item.research_question: How do electronegativity differences between mixed elements in high-entropy alloys (HEAs) influence charge redistribution and the specific adsorption of OH* and H* intermediates to overcome scaling relations in water splitting?
item.material_system: FeCoNiXRu (X: Cu, Cr, Mn) high-entropy alloy nanoparticles supported on carbon nanofibers (FeCoNiXRu/CNFs), specifically FeCoNiMnRu with composition Fe0.23Co0.22Ni0.22Mn0.14Ru0.19
item.processing_route: Electrospinning of metal salt/PAN polymer solution followed by graphitization in a chemical vapor deposition furnace; pre-oxidation at 230 °C for 3 h, then heating to 1000 °C under Ar atmosphere for 3 h at 2 °C min−1
item.test_conditions: Alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) and oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in Ar-saturated 1.0 M KOH electrolyte at 25 °C; overall water splitting in a two-electrode system; stability tests up to 600 h at 1 A cm−2 and 100 h at 1000 mA cm−2
key_findings: FeCoNiMnRu/CNFs achieved the lowest overpotential of 71 mV to produce a current density of 100 mA cm−2 for HER, significantly lower than Ru/CNFs (421 mV) and FeCoNi/CNFs (410 mV).
The Tafel slope for FeCoNiMnRu/CNFs was 67.4 mV dec−1, indicating a Volmer–Heyrovsky mechanism.
DFT calculations identified the Co site as the most active center for water dissociation with the lowest energy barrier of 0.34 eV.
Ru sites exhibited the most appealing Gibbs free energy of hydrogen adsorption (ΔGH*) of −0.07 eV, making them the preferred sites for H* adsorption.
Operando Raman spectroscopy confirmed the formation of Ru-H* intermediates at 2069 and 2092 cm−1, which were absent in samples without Ru.
Decreasing the electronegativity of the fifth metal (from Cu to Mn) reduced the energy barriers for water dissociation and H* adsorption.
The FeCoNiMnRu/CNFs||FeCoNiMnRu/CNFs electrolyzer system required only 1.65 V to achieve 100 mA cm−2 for overall water splitting.
The catalyst maintained a stable current density of 1 A cm−2 for over 600 h in 1.0 M KOH without structural degradation.
item.mechanism: Electronegativity differences between the mixed elements (Fe: 1.83, Co: 1.88, Ni: 1.91, Mn: 1.55, Ru: 2.20) induce significant charge redistribution, causing electron transfer from Fe, Co, Ni, and Mn to Ru. This creates highly active Co sites optimized for water dissociation (stabilizing OH*) and Ru sites optimized for H* adsorption, allowing simultaneous stabilization of multiple intermediates and breaking scaling relations.
item.limitations: The text does not explicitly state limitations of the study.
item.future_work: The work opens up a fascinating direction for breaking scaling relation issues for multistep reactions by constructing controllable multifunctional active sites on HEA surfaces.
quotes: The electronegativity differences between mixed elements in HEA induce significant charge redistribution and create highly active Co and Ru sites with optimized energy barriers for simultaneously stabilizing OH* and H* intermediates.
In the FeCoNiMnRu NP, the Co sites are the most active centers with the lowest energy barrier (0.34 eV) for water dissociation.
During the subsequent H* adsorption/desorption process, H* leaves Co and is absorbed on Ru sites, which exhibit the lowest ΔGH* of −0.07 eV.

item.processing_route: First-principles Spin-polarization density functional theory (DFT) calculations within the generalized gradient approximation (GGA) using the Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) formulation with vdW corrections, projected augmented wave (PAW) potentials, plane wave basis set with a kinetic energy cutoff of 400 eV, Gaussian smearing method with a width of 0.05 eV, 15 Å vacuum spacing, 3 × 3 × 1 Monkhorst-Pack k-point sampling, and DFT + U correction for ZPE calculation using 6 × 2 × 2 Monkhorst-Pack k-points
item.test_conditions: Self-consistent electronic energy when energy change was smaller than 10−6 eV; geometry optimization convergent when energy change was smaller than 0.04 eV Å−1
key_findings: DFT + U correction used in systems for ZPE calculation
quotes: We have employed the first-principles, to perform all Spin-polarization density functional theory (DFT) calculations within the generalized gradient approximation (GGA) using the Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) formulation.
In our alloy structure, the FCC structure has been obtained with the 80 atoms.
The ZPE has been calculation using the 6 × 2 × 2 Monkhorst-Pack k-point and DFT + U correction has been used in our systems.

records.text: Paper card. System: FCC structure with 80 atoms. Processing: First-principles Spin-polarization density functional theory (DFT) calculations within the generalized gradient approximation (GGA) using the Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) formulation with vdW corrections, projected augmented wave (PAW) potentials, plane wave basis set with a kinetic energy cutoff of 400 eV, Gaussian smearing method with a width of 0.05 eV, 15 Å vacuum spacing, 3 × 3 × 1 Monkhorst-Pack k-point sampling, and DFT + U correction for ZPE calculation using 6 × 2 × 2 Monkhorst-Pack k-points. Test conditions: Self-consistent electronic energy when energy change was smaller than 10−6 eV; geometry optimization convergent when energy change was smaller than 0.04 eV Å−1.
